title: Forming a cluster
text: A cluster needs at least three nodes. Set the same `cluster.cookie` on every node and list peers in `cluster.nodes`. Nodes must resolve each other by hostname; IP-only setups are not supported.

title: Split brain
text: If a network partition occurs the cluster pauses the minority side by default (`partition.strategy = pause_minority`). Paused nodes reject clients until the partition heals. Do not switch to `ignore` in production; it can cause divergent queues.

title: Rolling upgrades
text: Upgrade one node at a time, minor versions only (for example 3.2 to 3.3). Upgrading across a major version requires a full shutdown. Drain connections with `bin/quillbus drain` before stopping a node.

title: Connection limits
text: The setting `max_connections` in `conf/quillbus.conf` caps simultaneous client connections. The default is 1000. When the limit is reached new clients receive `CONNECTION_REFUSED: limit reached`. Raise the value together with the OS file descriptor limit (`ulimit -n`), which must be at least `max_connections * 2`.

title: Message retention
text: Messages are kept until consumed or until `retention.hours` expires (default 72). Setting `retention.hours = 0` disables expiry, which can fill the disk. Expired messages are moved to the dead-letter queue when `dlq.enabled = true`.

title: TLS
text: Enable TLS with `tls.enabled = true` and set `tls.keystore` and `tls.keystore.password`. Clients must then connect on port 5671. Certificates must use RSA 2048 bit or stronger; weaker keys are rejected at startup with `TLS_KEY_TOO_WEAK`.

title: Memory settings
text: The heap is set with `QB_HEAP` (for example `QB_HEAP=4g`). Do not set it above 75% of physical RAM, otherwise the OS may kill the process (OOM killer).

title: Installation
text: Sample documentation for the fictional product "Quillbus", a message broker. This knowledge base is bundled so the project runs offline.

title: System requirements
text: Quillbus 3.x requires Java 17 or newer and at least 4 GB of RAM. Java 11 is no longer supported since 3.0. On startup with an older Java version the broker exits with `UnsupportedClassVersionError`.

title: Installing on Linux
text: Download the tarball, extract it to `/opt/quillbus` and run `bin/quillbus start`. The broker listens on port 5672 for clients and 15672 for the management console. Create a dedicated `quillbus` system user; running as root is blocked by default.

title: Port already in use
text: If the broker fails with `Address already in use: 5672`, another process holds the client port. Find it with `ss -ltnp | grep 5672`, or change the port with `listener.port` in `conf/quillbus.conf` and restart.
Added `quillbus drain`. Fixed a memory leak in the management console when more than 500 queues exist. Default `ack.timeout` changed from 60 to 30 seconds.
Fixed `TLS_KEY_TOO_WEAK` being raised for valid ECDSA certificates. ECDSA P-256 keys are now accepted.
Dropped Java 11 support. Renamed `max_conn` to `max_connections`; the old name is ignored silently, so check your config after upgrading. Removed the legacy v1 client protocol.

title: Consumers stop receiving messages
text: If consumers stall while the queue depth grows, check for unacknowledged messages. A consumer that fetches messages but never acknowledges them holds them until `ack.timeout` (default 30 seconds). Lower `prefetch` to 10 and make sure the client calls `ack()` after processing. A stuck consumer can be identified in the management console under Connections, column `unacked`.

title: High memory usage
text: Memory grows when queues are unbounded. Set `queue.max_length` to cap queue size and choose `overflow = reject` or `overflow = drop_head`. Persistent queues with large backlogs also increase heap usage because the index is kept in memory.

title: Disk full alarm
text: When free disk space drops below `disk.free_limit` (default 1 GB) the broker blocks publishers and logs `DISK_ALARM`. Free space or raise the limit's headroom, then publishing resumes automatically. Check `retention.hours` if the disk fills repeatedly.

title: Slow publishing
text: Publisher throughput drops sharply when `sync_publish = true`, because every message waits for a disk flush. Use publisher confirms in batches, or set `sync_publish = false` if losing the last second of messages on a crash is acceptable.
